lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 17 and still lives at home with me. I wanted to check if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Since Alex is 17, there are specific rules that apply. You can normally qualify for Child Benefit for a child aged 16 or over (up to age 20) if they stay in approved education or training.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he in sixth form, college, doing A-levels, or in an approved training program?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's studying for his A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you! Alex being in sixth form studying for his A-levels would count as approved education.

Now I need to ask a few more questions to assess your eligibility:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to understand your responsibility for Alex:

**Do you live with Alex, or if not, are you contributing at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount towards his upkeep (such as for food, clothes, or pocket money)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you. Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** (For example, another parent or guardian?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One final question:

**Has Alex started paid work for 24 hours or more per week, started an apprenticeship, or started receiving benefits in his own right (such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't started any paid work, and he's not on an apprenticeship or receiving any benefits himself. He's just focused on his studies at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! **You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:
- You live in the UK and Alex lives at home with you, which means you're responsible for him
- Although Alex is 17, he qualifies because he's in approved education (studying A-levels at sixth form college)
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him
- He hasn't started full-time work (24+ hours per week), an apprenticeship, or started receiving benefits in his own right

**Important things to note:**
- You can continue to receive Child Benefit for Alex as long as he remains in approved education or training, up until he turns 20
- If Alex's circumstances change (for example, if he leaves education, starts working 24+ hours per week, or starts claiming benefits), you'll need to notify HMRC
- If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge

If you haven't already claimed, you can apply for Child Benefit. If you have any other questions, feel free to ask!
